title: Codex Task
summary: <task> Deep technical analysis of why block-level D-stage optimization in SVD-LLM compression...

result.rawOutput:
The code does not suggest a RoPE wiring bug. The stronger explanation is objective mismatch: Level 2 minimizes block-output squared error on the current frontier state, but it never constrains the RoPE-shaped `QK^T` geometry directly. In this repo that is exactly what happens in [block_minimax.py](/home/xiyaofeng/huicheng/SVD_LLM/src/compress/block_minimax.py#L28), [block_forward.py](/home/xiyaofeng/huicheng/SVD_LLM/src/compress/block_forward.py#L47), [compress_model.py](/home/xiyaofeng/huicheng/SVD_LLM/src/compress/compress_model.py#L930), and the paper objective in [main.tex](/home/xiyaofeng/huicheng/SVD_LLM/paper/block-granularity/main.tex#L294).

1. The `rope_theta -> correlated error -> coherent amplification` theory is directionally right, but the current version is too strong.
The good part is that Mistral and Qwen both use `rope_theta=1e6` with standard RoPE, while LLaMA uses `1e4` and MiniCPM uses `1e4` plus custom longrope scaling in [Mistral config](/home/xiyaofeng/huicheng/SVD_LLM/Mistral-7B-v0.3/config.json#L18), [Qwen config](/home/xiyaofeng/huicheng/SVD_LLM/Qwen2.5-7B/config.json#L19), and [MiniCPM config](/home/xiyaofeng/huicheng/SVD_LLM/models/MiniCPM4-8B/config.json#L36). With head_dim 128 in all four models, the only big RoPE difference is effectively `theta`. Using the HF formula in [modeling_mistral.py](/home/xiyaofeng/huicheng/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/transformers/models/mistral/modeling_mistral.py#L305), over a 2048-token calibration window about 52% of RoPE bands at `theta=1e6` rotate less than `pi` total, versus about 28% at `theta=1e4`. That means the 1M models excite much less positional phase diversity during calibration, so position-sensitive Q/K errors are less observable to the block MSE objective.

The flaw is that “adjacent positions have ~100x smaller rotations” is not literally true for all bands. The highest-frequency bands are unchanged; only the slower bands are much slower. So I would not write “positions become nearly indistinguishable.” I would write: high `rope_theta` compresses positional phase variation over the 2048-token calibration window, making low-rank Q/K errors more position-uniform and therefore more likely to accumulate coherently.

2. The original Mistral does not fail because high `theta` is not itself unstable; the compressed Q/K/V/O geometry is.
All three LLaMA-family implementations apply RoPE in the standard way before attention, and I checked the helper functions are effectively the same in [modeling_llama.py](/home/xiyaofeng/huicheng/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/transformers/models/llama/modeling_llama.py#L145) and [modeling_qwen2.py](/home/xiyaofeng/huicheng/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/transformers/models/qwen2/modeling_qwen2.py#L123). The pretrained model has weights jointly trained for that geometry. Level 2 replaces all seven sublayers with low-rank factors and only asks for local block-output agreement, so it can preserve `h_out` on calibration samples while still breaking delicate Q/K alignment, head-group calibration, and softmax margins. The strong F-stage recovery in your table supports that interpretation: the model is not inherently unstable, but D is landing in a locally good, globally brittle basin.

3. The most plausible alternative is not “GQA alone,” but “high theta + GQA + no residual damping + short-window local loss.”
GQA is clearly relevant because `repeat_kv` broadcasts K/V errors across query heads in [block_forward.py](/home/xiyaofeng/huicheng/SVD_LLM/src/compress/block_forward.py#L150). LLaMA has MHA, so K/V error is head-local. Mistral and Qwen share K/V across 4 and 7 query heads. But GQA alone cannot explain the split, because MiniCPM is the most extreme GQA case and still works. The missing ingredient is that MiniCPM also damps both residual branches by `scale_depth / sqrt(L)` in [block_forward.py](/home/xiyaofeng/huicheng/SVD_LLM/src/compress/block_forward.py#L87) and [modeling_minicpm.py](/home/xiyaofeng/huicheng/SVD_LLM/models/MiniCPM4-8B/modeling_minicpm.py#L1603). Numerically that is about `1.4 / sqrt(32) ~= 0.247`, which is a real anti-amplification mechanism. So the bad combination looks like high-theta RoPE plus shared K/V plus full-strength residual accumulation.

4. If LLaMA shows much higher SNR than Mistral, that supports a scale/conditioning story, but it does not by itself settle the RoPE question.
One important code fact: your “block MSE” is not elementwise MSE. `_domain_loss_value()` sums squared error over hidden dimension and divides only by token count in [block_minimax.py](/home/xiyaofeng/huicheng/SVD_LLM/src/compress/block_minimax.py#L55). So absolute loss is architecture-scale dependent. That is why Mistral can have far smaller block losses than LLaMA or MiniCPM and still much worse PPL. If LLaMA has better properly normalized block-output or attention-logit SNR, that means magnitude matters. To confirm the coherence theory, you need a magnitude-independent test: compare correlation of attention-logit error across query positions, or compare attention KL at matched normalized Q/K error. Similar normalized error but much higher position-wise correlation on 1M-theta models would be the clean confirmation.

5. The hidden-state norm growth is not automatically a smoking gun.
Your logged `17 -> 34 -> 61 -> 119` for Mistral comes from the frontier cache after previous compressed blocks have already been installed, so it is a compressed-chain statistic, not a pure original-model baseline. Some residual growth is normal in these decoders; LLaMA and MiniCPM can also have very large late-block losses without catastrophic PPL. I would call the growth “a warning sign only if it is materially steeper than the original-model frontier.” The right control is to log the same norms from an uncompressed `orig_cache` path, not to interpret the raw doubling by itself.

6. Practical implications.
For the paper, I would not claim a generic RoPE instability. I would claim: “On high-`theta` RoPE models, 2048-token local block reconstruction underconstrains attention geometry; combined with GQA and full residual gain, this makes Level 2 more likely to introduce coherent Q/K errors that accumulate across blocks.”

For the method, the safest short-term policy is:
- Skip D for `rope_theta >= 1e6` and go `B -> F`, or at least test that path before keeping D.
- If you keep D, protect attention first: freeze or up-rank `q_proj` and `k_proj`, or run D only on `v/o/mlp`.
- Use longer calibration contexts or mixed position windows for high-theta models.
- Change the loss, not the runtime model: use relative block loss and add a RoPE-aware attention-logit or attention-KL term after rotation.
- Do not normalize hidden states between blocks at inference. That changes the pretrained function. If you want normalization, normalize the objective or add a teacher-norm penalty.

The single best verification experiment is: keep the exact D pipeline, but for Mistral/Qwen run `D_without_qk` and `B->F`. If those stop the collapse, the failure mode is almost certainly in RoPE-sensitive Q/K geometry rather than generic low-rank optimization.
